title: Principles for Prompt Engineering - Karina Nguyen (Claude Instant @ Anthropic)
talk_summary: Karina Nguyen presents Claude-specific prompt-engineering mechanisms: consistent XML structure, task placement at the end of long context, evidence quoting, decomposition, self-consistency, and LLM-generated evals. Most are old Claude anecdotes, but several are directly copyable into agent prompt templates, PR review gates, and regression evals.

takeaways.technique: Put task instructions after long context
takeaways.what_they_do: For long-document Q&A, place the document/context first and the question/instructions at the end; ask the model to pull relevant quotes into thought/critique tags before answering.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for document Q&A asking the question at the end of The Prompt performs a lot better than asking at the beginning
takeaways.numbers: Tested 70k and 95k token documents; end placement mattered more than other optimization strategies.

takeaways.technique: Evidence-gated review with explicit no-evidence fallback
takeaways.what_they_do: Require the model to quote directly from the source document; if no relevant quote exists, instruct it to say it found no relevant quotes rather than fabricate support.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if there are no quotes in this document that seems relevant to this question please just say I don't find any relevant quotes

takeaways.what_they_do: Generate multiple independent samples and take the majority answer, or use another model to check whether samples are consistent and deselect inconsistent ones.
takeaways.evidence_quote: have like two generated samples and ask another model to evaluate whether those samples are consistent or not

takeaways.what_they_do: Ask the model to split a complex question into independent, self-contained subquestions, answer each in separate context, then recompose the answers for the final decision.
takeaways.evidence_quote: decompose a question into like multiple sub questions so that each sub question are kind of independent from each other

takeaways.what_they_do: Put every input and output section in consistent XML tags; the speaker says Claude was fine-tuned on XML and it is easier to extract than markdown/JSON.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Claude really likes XML tags really loves XML tags
takeaways.numbers: Anecdotal: 'almost 100% accuracy' with XML vs markdown/JSON.

takeaways.technique: LLM-generated regression evals from source docs
takeaways.what_they_do: Split documents into sections, use an LLM to generate multiple-choice questions with wrong answers, reassemble randomized long documents, and test recall across prompt variants and answer positions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: split the document into sections and use claw to generate like five multiple choice questions for each section
takeaways.numbers: Tested 70k and 95k token documents; answer position beginning/middle/end was varied.
